# gh-1107: SM: check-run stamps fail with 'Bad substitution' — job names interpolated into shell string

## Description

## Goal — validation check-run stamps never break on job names (v1)
One sentence: **the SM stamps the required validation check-runs on every PR head regardless of what characters the dispatched run's job names contain.**

`stampValidationChecksForModule` (`js/smAgent.js` ~7570–7620) builds `gh api -X POST .../check-runs -f summary="<jobs table>"` as a shell string with values inside **double quotes**. The summary contains job names from the dispatched run; flutter_agent_harness has a job literally named `Lockfile smoke (${{ matrix.os }} release)`. `/bin/sh` (dash) sees `${{ ... }}` → `Bad substitution`, exit 2, and **no stamp is written**. Live 2026-10-19 17:15:
```
⚠️ stamp "Quality gate" on 26203e9: ... exit code 2: /tmp/dmtools_cli_….sh: 2: Bad substitution
⚠️ stamp "JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)" ...   ⚠️ stamp "Binaries smoke gate" ...
```
Missing stamps keep required checks "expected" → PRs BLOCKED (bridge-free mode, factory #510).

## Why this framing
The bug is not about one job name; any `$`, backtick, `"` or `\` in name, title, summary or details URL is shell-interpreted. This is also an injection surface: job names come from repo workflow files a PR can edit.

## Architecture
- Build the request body as JSON (`{name, head_sha, status, conclusion?, details_url?, output:{title, summary}}`), write it to a temp file, call `gh api -X POST repos/{o}/{r}/check-runs --input <file>`; delete the file in `finally`.
- Invariant: **zero untrusted bytes inside the shell command string** — only the fixed repo path and temp-file path.
- Audit all other `cli_execute_command` call sites that interpolate PR/run-derived text into `"…"` (titles, comments, branch names) and convert them the same way or to single-quote escaping via one helper `shellQuote()`.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — stamping with a summary containing `${{ matrix.os }}`, `$(id)`, backticks, `"`, `\`, newlines succeeds and the posted body equals the input byte-for-byte (UT-1).
- **AC2** — the command string passed to `cli_execute_command` contains none of the summary/title/name bytes (UT-2, byte-scan).
- **AC3** — temp file removed on success and failure (UT-3).
- **AC4** — dry-run path unchanged (REG-1).
- **AC5** — audit list of converted call sites in the PR description; each gets a test with a hostile string (UT-4..n).

## Edge cases
- **E1** — summary > 65535 chars (GitHub output limit) → truncated with a marker, not rejected.
- **E2** — temp dir not writable → warn and skip, same as today's failure mode.

## Non-goals
- Changing which checks are stamped or their names.

## References
- factory #510 (bridge-free stamps); IstiN/flutter_agent_harness run 39290439628.

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm. The SAME budget bounds
 *   the red-gate rework arm (rule.redHeadGated — rework-on-red-gate-unlatched, gh-917):
 *   that arm_rework path records the shared 🔴 marker history and, at redHeadCap reds
 *   on an unchanged head, withholds the arm and escalates the owner once per head
 *   (🛑 marker comment — no infinite retry on unfixable-without-toolchain violations).
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.noopLapMax (default 2, gh-957) — the THREADS-armed twin of the

# gh-1107: SM: check-run stamps fail with 'Bad substitution' — job names interpolated into shell string

## Description

## Goal — validation check-run stamps never break on job names (v1)
One sentence: **the SM stamps the required validation check-runs on every PR head regardless of what characters the dispatched run's job names contain.**

`stampValidationChecksForModule` (`js/smAgent.js` ~7570–7620) builds `gh api -X POST .../check-runs -f summary="<jobs table>"` as a shell string with values inside **double quotes**. The summary contains job names from the dispatched run; flutter_agent_harness has a job literally named `Lockfile smoke (${{ matrix.os }} release)`. `/bin/sh` (dash) sees `${{ ... }}` → `Bad substitution`, exit 2, and **no stamp is written**. Live 2026-10-19 17:15:
```
⚠️ stamp "Quality gate" on 26203e9: ... exit code 2: /tmp/dmtools_cli_….sh: 2: Bad substitution
⚠️ stamp "JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)" ...   ⚠️ stamp "Binaries smoke gate" ...
```
Missing stamps keep required checks "expected" → PRs BLOCKED (bridge-free mode, factory #510).

## Why this framing
The bug is not about one job name; any `$`, backtick, `"` or `\` in name, title, summary or details URL is shell-interpreted. This is also an injection surface: job names come from repo workflow files a PR can edit.

## Architecture
- Build the request body as JSON (`{name, head_sha, status, conclusion?, details_url?, output:{title, summary}}`), write it to a temp file, call `gh api -X POST repos/{o}/{r}/check-runs --input <file>`; delete the file in `finally`.
- Invariant: **zero untrusted bytes inside the shell command string** — only the fixed repo path and temp-file path.
- Audit all other `cli_execute_command` call sites that interpolate PR/run-derived text into `"…"` (titles, comments, branch names) and convert them the same way or to single-quote escaping via one helper `shellQuote()`.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — stamping with a summary containing `${{ matrix.os }}`, `$(id)`, backticks, `"`, `\`, newlines succeeds and the posted body equals the input byte-for-byte (UT-1).
- **AC2** — the command string passed to `cli_execute_command` contains none of the summary/title/name bytes (UT-2, byte-scan).
- **AC3** — temp file removed on success and failure (UT-3).
- **AC4** — dry-run path unchanged (REG-1).
- **AC5** — audit list of converted call sites in the PR description; each gets a test with a hostile string (UT-4..n).

## Edge cases
- **E1** — summary > 65535 chars (GitHub output limit) → truncated with a marker, not rejected.
- **E2** — temp dir not writable → warn and skip, same as today's failure mode.

## Non-goals
- Changing which checks are stamped or their names.

## References
- factory #510 (bridge-free stamps); IstiN/flutter_agent_harness run 39290439628.

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,

/**
 * Factory token usage — per-leg token-usage publisher (owner directive
 * 2026-10-13: factory glue moves into dmtools-agents as JS agent code; awf
 * workflows become thin callers).
 *
 * JS port of the awf factory-teammate.yml step «Publish leg token usage
 * (fa-tokens ledger -> factory-data)» — byte-extracted into
 * scripts/publish-token-usage.sh by IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows#34.
 * Behavior contract is identical:
 *
 *   1. Read the run output (RUN_OUTPUT). Missing/empty → skip (warn).
 *   2. Sum every `fa-tokens: {…}` ledger line (resume-aware: one line per
 *      session segment) — balanced-brace scan so a payload wrapped in a log
 *      line is found whole; invalid payloads are skipped. input/output/
 *      cacheRead are summed; the last-seen model wins. Zero in+out → skip.
 *   3. Leg: the run guard collapses the rework slot into kind="dev", so the
 *      true leg is recovered from the runner-config basename — *rework* →
 *      "rework", else KIND, else "dev".
 *   4. Anchor → key: pr-* passes through; gh-N → issue-N; anything else →
 *      skip (warn).
 *   5. Row (printf field order): {"leg","at","prompt","completion","total",
 *      "cacheRead","model"} — at = UTC ISO-8601 seconds.
 *   6. Bootstrap the factory-data branch from the default-branch head
 *      (422 "already exists" is the normal case), then up to 3 attempts:
 *      GET contents (sha + body), append the row under the key, drop rows
 *      older than 14 days, keep the last 40 per key, drop emptied keys,
 *      PUT Contents API with the existing sha. Conflict → refetch → retry
 *      (sh backoff attempt*2s). Exhausted → warn; rows are decorative and
 *      the next leg retries.
 *
 * Transport mirrors factoryState.js: every command starts with `gh` (the
 * executor whitelists the first token); base64 stays in-shell
 * (`printf %s … | base64` / `--jq .content | base64 -d`) so the JS side
 * never needs a base64 codec.
 *
 * Env/file contract (the sh step's env block; the JSRunner entry reads
 * jobParams.customParams first, these env names as fallback):
 *   RUN_OUTPUT   path of the captured run output (fa-tokens ledger source)
 *   CONFIG       runner config path; basename minus .json decides the leg
 *   KIND         leg kind when the basename has no "rework" (default "dev")
 *   ANCHOR       work anchor: pr-<n> | gh-<n>
 *   REPO         owner/repo of the factory-data target
 *   DATA_BRANCH  target branch (default "factory-data")
 *   DATA_PATH    target path   (default "data/fa-tokens.json")
 *
 * Pure functions carry no IO: the publisher takes { exec, read, sleepMs,
 * log } capturers (factoryState.js convention) so tests mock the transport
 * via loadModule without touching any global.

# gh-1107: SM: check-run stamps fail with 'Bad substitution' — job names interpolated into shell string

## Description

## Goal — validation check-run stamps never break on job names (v1)
One sentence: **the SM stamps the required validation check-runs on every PR head regardless of what characters the dispatched run's job names contain.**

`stampValidationChecksForModule` (`js/smAgent.js` ~7570–7620) builds `gh api -X POST .../check-runs -f summary="<jobs table>"` as a shell string with values inside **double quotes**. The summary contains job names from the dispatched run; flutter_agent_harness has a job literally named `Lockfile smoke (${{ matrix.os }} release)`. `/bin/sh` (dash) sees `${{ ... }}` → `Bad substitution`, exit 2, and **no stamp is written**. Live 2026-10-19 17:15:
```
⚠️ stamp "Quality gate" on 26203e9: ... exit code 2: /tmp/dmtools_cli_….sh: 2: Bad substitution
⚠️ stamp "JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)" ...   ⚠️ stamp "Binaries smoke gate" ...
```
Missing stamps keep required checks "expected" → PRs BLOCKED (bridge-free mode, factory #510).

## Why this framing
The bug is not about one job name; any `$`, backtick, `"` or `\` in name, title, summary or details URL is shell-interpreted. This is also an injection surface: job names come from repo workflow files a PR can edit.

## Architecture
- Build the request body as JSON (`{name, head_sha, status, conclusion?, details_url?, output:{title, summary}}`), write it to a temp file, call `gh api -X POST repos/{o}/{r}/check-runs --input <file>`; delete the file in `finally`.
- Invariant: **zero untrusted bytes inside the shell command string** — only the fixed repo path and temp-file path.
- Audit all other `cli_execute_command` call sites that interpolate PR/run-derived text into `"…"` (titles, comments, branch names) and convert them the same way or to single-quote escaping via one helper `shellQuote()`.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — stamping with a summary containing `${{ matrix.os }}`, `$(id)`, backticks, `"`, `\`, newlines succeeds and the posted body equals the input byte-for-byte (UT-1).
- **AC2** — the command string passed to `cli_execute_command` contains none of the summary/title/name bytes (UT-2, byte-scan).
- **AC3** — temp file removed on success and failure (UT-3).
- **AC4** — dry-run path unchanged (REG-1).
- **AC5** — audit list of converted call sites in the PR description; each gets a test with a hostile string (UT-4..n).

## Edge cases
- **E1** — summary > 65535 chars (GitHub output limit) → truncated with a marker, not rejected.
- **E2** — temp dir not writable → warn and skip, same as today's failure mode.

## Non-goals
- Changing which checks are stamped or their names.

## References
- factory #510 (bridge-free stamps); IstiN/flutter_agent_harness run 39290439628.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

 * Behavior contract is identical:
 *
 *   1. Read the run output (RUN_OUTPUT). Missing/empty → skip (warn).
 *   2. Sum every `fa-tokens: {…}` ledger line (resume-aware: one line per
 *      session segment) — balanced-brace scan so a payload wrapped in a log
 *      line is found whole; invalid payloads are skipped. input/output/
 *      cacheRead are summed; the last-seen model wins. Zero in+out → skip.
 *   3. Leg: the run guard collapses the rework slot into kind="dev", so the
 *      true leg is recovered from the runner-config basename — *rework* →
 *      "rework", else KIND, else "dev".
 *   4. Anchor → key: pr-* passes through; gh-N → issue-N; anything else →
 *      skip (warn).
 *   5. Row (printf field order): {"leg","at","prompt","completion","total",
 *      "cacheRead","model"} — at = UTC ISO-8601 seconds.
 *   6. Bootstrap the factory-data branch from the default-branch head
 *      (422 "already exists" is the normal case), then up to 3 attempts:
 *      GET contents (sha + body), append the row under the key, drop rows
 *      older than 14 days, keep the last 40 per key, drop emptied keys,
 *      PUT Contents API with the existing sha. Conflict → refetch → retry
 *      (sh backoff attempt*2s). Exhausted → warn; rows are decorative and
 *      the next leg retries.

 * executor whitelists the first token); base64 stays in-shell

 *   RUN_OUTPUT   path of the captured run output (fa-tokens ledger source)

 *   ANCHOR       work anchor: pr-<n> | gh-<n>
 *   REPO         owner/repo of the factory-data target
 *   DATA_BRANCH  target branch (default "factory-data")
 *   DATA_PATH    target path   (default "data/fa-tokens.json")

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

{"path":"input/gh-1107/ticket.json"}
{"command":"git status && git log --oneline -5 && git branch -a | head -20"}

{
  "key": "gh-1107",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "SM: check-run stamps fail with 'Bad substitution' — job names interpolated into shell string",
    "description": "## Goal — validation check-run stamps never break on job names (v1)
One sentence: **the SM stamps the required validation check-runs on every PR head regardless of what characters the dispatched run's job names contain.**

`stampValidationChecksForModule` (`js/smAgent.js` ~7570–7620) builds `gh api -X POST .../check-runs -f summary="<jobs table>"` as a shell string with values inside **double quotes**. The summary contains job names from the dispatched run; flutter_agent_harness has a job literally named `Lockfile smoke (${{ matrix.os }} release)`. `/bin/sh` (dash) sees `${{ ... }}` → `Bad substitution`, exit 2, and **no stamp is written**. Live 2026-10-19 17:15:
```
⚠️ stamp "Quality gate" on 26203e9: ... exit code 2: /tmp/dmtools_cli_….sh: 2: Bad substitution
⚠️ stamp "JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)" ...   ⚠️ stamp "Binaries smoke gate" ...
```
Missing stamps keep required checks "expected" → PRs BLOCKED (bridge-free mode, factory #510).

## Why this framing
The bug is not about one job name; any `$`, backtick, `"` or `\` in name, title, summary or details URL is shell-interpreted. This is also an injection surface: job names come from repo workflow files a PR can edit.

## Architecture
- Build the request body as JSON (`{name, head_sha, status, conclusion?, details_url?, output:{title, summary}}`), write it to a temp file, call `gh api -X POST repos/{o}/{r}/check-runs --input <file>`; delete the file in `finally`.
- Invariant: **zero untrusted bytes inside the shell command string** — only the fixed repo path and temp-file path.
- Audit all other `cli_execute_command` call sites that interpolate PR/run-derived text into `"…"` (titles, comments, branch names) and convert them the same way or to single-quote escaping via one helper `shellQuote()`.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — stamping with a summary containing `${{ matrix.os }}`, `$(id)`, backticks, `"`, `\`, newlines succeeds and the posted body equals the input byte-for-byte (UT-1).
- **AC2** — the command string passed to `cli_execute_command` contains none of the summary/title/name bytes (UT-2, byte-scan).
- **AC3** — temp file removed on success and failure (UT-3).
- **AC4** — dry-run path unchanged (REG-1).
- **AC5** — audit list of converted call sites in the PR description; each gets a test with a hostile string (UT-4..n).

## Edge cases
- **E1** — summary > 65535 chars (GitHub output limit) → truncated with a marker, not rejected.
- **E2** — temp dir not writable → warn and skip, same as today's failure mode.

## Non-goals
- Changing which checks are stamped or their names.

## References
- factory #510 (bridge-free stamps); IstiN/flutter_agent_harness run 39290439628."
  }
}

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.

 *      session segment) — balanced-brace scan so a payload wrapped in a log

 *      cacheRead are summed; the last-seen model wins. Zero in+out → skip.

{
  "key": "gh-1107",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "SM: check-run stamps fail with 'Bad substitution' — job names interpolated into shell string",
    "description": "## Goal — validation check-run stamps never break on job names (v1)
One sentence: **the SM stamps the required validation check-runs on every PR head regardless of what characters the dispatched run's job names contain.**

`stampValidationChecksForModule` (`js/smAgent.js` ~7570–7620) builds `gh api -X POST .../check-runs -f summary="<jobs table>"` as a shell string with values inside **double quotes**. The summary contains job names from the dispatched run; flutter_agent_harness has a job literally named `Lockfile smoke (${{ matrix.os }} release)`. `/bin/sh` (dash) sees `${{ ... }}` → `Bad substitution`, exit 2, and **no stamp is written**. Live 2026-10-19 17:15:
```
⚠️ stamp "Quality gate" on 26203e9: ... exit code 2: /tmp/dmtools_cli_….sh: 2: Bad substitution
⚠️ stamp "JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)" ...   ⚠️ stamp "Binaries smoke gate" ...
```
Missing stamps keep required checks "expected" → PRs BLOCKED (bridge-free mode, factory #510).

## Why this framing
The bug is not about one job name; any `$`, backtick, `"` or `\` in name, title, summary or details URL is shell-interpreted. This is also an injection surface: job names come from repo workflow files a PR can edit.

## Architecture
- Build the request body as JSON (`{name, head_sha, status, conclusion?, details_url?, output:{title, summary}}`), write it to a temp file, call `gh api -X POST repos/{o}/{r}/check-runs --input <file>`; delete the file in `finally`.
- Invariant: **zero untrusted bytes inside the shell command string** — only the fixed repo path and temp-file path.
- Audit all other `cli_execute_command` call sites that interpolate PR/run-derived text into `"…"` (titles, comments, branch names) and convert them the same way or to single-quote escaping via one helper `shellQuote()`.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — stamping with a summary containing `${{ matrix.os }}`, `$(id)`, backticks, `"`, `\`, newlines succeeds and the posted body equals the input byte-for-byte (UT-1).
- **AC2** — the command string passed to `cli_execute_command` contains none of the summary/title/name bytes (UT-2, byte-scan).
- **AC3** — temp file removed on success and failure (UT-3).
- **AC4** — dry-run path unchanged (REG-1).
- **AC5** — audit list of converted call sites in the PR description; each gets a test with a hostile string (UT-4..n).

## Edge cases
- **E1** — summary > 65535 chars (GitHub output limit) → truncated with a marker, not rejected.
- **E2** — temp dir not writable → warn and skip, same as today's failure mode.

## Non-goals
- Changing which checks are stamped or their names.

## References
- factory #510 (bridge-free stamps); IstiN/flutter_agent_harness run 39290439628."
  }
}

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm. The SAME budget bounds
 *   the red-gate rework arm (rule.redHeadGated — rework-on-red-gate-unlatched, gh-917):
 *   that arm_rework path records the shared 🔴 marker history and, at redHeadCap reds
 *   on an unchanged head, withholds the arm and escalates the owner once per head
 *   (🛑 marker comment — no infinite retry on unfixable-without-toolchain violations).
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.noopLapMax (default 2, gh-957) — the THREADS-armed twin of the
 *   empty-lap cap, bound on the lap markers pushReworkChanges stamps per leg
 *   close ({head, pushed, resolved}): after this many consecutive laps on
 *   the SAME head with ZERO pushed commits AND ZERO resolved threads, the
 *   arm_rework action AND the restore_rework_arm sweep withhold the arm and
 *   escalate the owner once per head (label rework-loop-escalated + 🛑
 *   comment) instead of re-arming forever (live dart #424: 7 no-op legs / 2h
 *   starved the whole queue). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a
 *   new head, resets the budget by construction.
 *   jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs (default 45000, gh-848) — the
 *   twin-guard cancel polls a selected stale run until its jobs materialize

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm. The SAME budget bounds
 *   the red-gate rework arm (rule.redHeadGated — rework-on-red-gate-unlatched, gh-917):
 *   that arm_rework path records the shared 🔴 marker history and, at redHeadCap reds
 *   on an unchanged head, withholds the arm and escalates the owner once per head
 *   (🛑 marker comment — no infinite retry on unfixable-without-toolchain violations).
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many

 *      session segment) — balanced-brace scan so a payload wrapped in a log

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm. The SAME budget bounds
 *   the red-gate rework arm (rule.redHeadGated — rework-on-red-gate-unlatched, gh-917):
 *   that arm_rework path records the shared 🔴 marker history and, at redHeadCap reds
 *   on an unchanged head, withholds the arm and escalates the owner once per head
 *   (🛑 marker comment — no infinite retry on unfixable-without-toolchain violations).
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.noopLapMax (default 2, gh-957) — the THREADS-armed twin of the
 *   empty-lap cap, bound on the lap markers pushReworkChanges stamps per leg
 *   close ({head, pushed, resolved}): after this many consecutive laps on
 *   the SAME head with ZERO pushed commits AND ZERO resolved threads, the
 *   arm_rework action AND the restore_rework_arm sweep withhold the arm and
 *   escalate the owner once per head (label rework-loop-escalated + 🛑
 *   comment) instead of re-arming forever (live dart #424: 7 no-op legs / 2h
 *   starved the whole queue). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a
 *   new head, resets the budget by construction.
 *   jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs (default 45000, gh-848) — the
 *   twin-guard cancel polls a selected stale run until its jobs materialize
 *   (run.status != 'queued') up to this long before cancelling; still
 *   queued → the cancel is DEFERRED to the next tick. A queued cancel
 *   orphans the run's registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts that
 *   seize the merge gate forever (live fa #1457/#1520, ghosts #4-#6).
 *   0 restores the legacy cancel-immediately behavior. jobParams.
 *   cancelMaterializePollMs (default 3000, gh-848) — the poll interval.
 *   jobParams.dispatchRaceGraceMs (default 60000, gh-748) — how long a COMPLETED
 *   run on the head still counts as "may have just ordered CI" for the validate_pr
 *   dispatch-race guard: before dispatching, the arm also counts ANY run on the
 *   head_sha (any workflow/event/actor — the kicker's own push run included) that

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm. The SAME budget bounds
 *   the red-gate rework arm (rule.redHeadGated — rework-on-red-gate-unlatched, gh-917):
 *   that arm_rework path records the shared 🔴 marker history and, at redHeadCap reds
 *   on an unchanged head, withholds the arm and escalates the owner once per head
 *   (🛑 marker comment — no infinite retry on unfixable-without-toolchain violations).
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.noopLapMax (default 2, gh-957) — the THREADS-armed twin of the
 *   empty-lap cap, bound on the lap markers pushReworkChanges stamps per leg
 *   close ({head, pushed, resolved}): after this many consecutive laps on
 *   the SAME head with ZERO pushed commits AND ZERO resolved threads, the
 *   arm_rework action AND the restore_rework_arm sweep withhold the arm and
 *   escalate the owner once per head (label rework-loop-escalated + 🛑
 *   comment) instead of re-arming forever (live dart #424: 7 no-op legs / 2h
 *   starved the whole queue). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a

 *      session segment) — balanced-brace scan so a payload wrapped in a log

 *      cacheRead are summed; the last-seen model wins. Zero in+out → skip.
 *   3. Leg: the run guard collapses the rework slot into kind="dev", so the

 *      skip (warn).

 *      "cacheRead","model"} — at = UTC ISO-8601 seconds.

 *      (422 "already exists" is the normal case), then up to 3 attempts:
 *      GET contents (sha + body), append the row under the key, drop rows
 *      older than 14 days, keep the last 40 per key, drop emptied keys,
 *      PUT Contents API with the existing sha. Conflict → refetch → retry
 *      (sh backoff attempt*2s). Exhausted → warn; rows are decorative and
 *      the next leg retries.

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm. The SAME budget bounds
 *   the red-gate rework arm (rule.redHeadGated — rework-on-red-gate-unlatched, gh-917):
 *   that arm_rework path records the shared 🔴 marker history and, at redHeadCap reds
 *   on an unchanged head, withholds the arm and escalates the owner once per head
 *   (🛑 marker comment — no infinite retry on unfixable-without-toolchain violations).
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.noopLapMax (default 2, gh-957) — the THREADS-armed twin of the
 *   empty-lap cap, bound on the lap markers pushReworkChanges stamps per leg
 *   close ({head, pushed, resolved}): after this many consecutive laps on

 *   arm_rework action AND the restore_rework_arm sweep withhold the arm and
 *   escalate the owner once per head (label rework-loop-escalated + 🛑
 *   comment) instead of re-arming forever (live dart #424: 7 no-op legs / 2h
 *   starved the whole queue). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a
 *   new head, resets the budget by construction.
 *   jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs (default 45000, gh-848) — the
 *   twin-guard cancel polls a selected stale run until its jobs materialize
