/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm. The SAME budget bounds
 *   the red-gate rework arm (rule.redHeadGated — rework-on-red-gate-unlatched, gh-917):
 *   that arm_rework path records the shared 🔴 marker history and, at redHeadCap reds
 *   on an unchanged head, withholds the arm and escalates the owner once per head
 *   (🛑 marker comment — no infinite retry on unfixable-without-toolchain violations).
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.noopLapMax (default 2, gh-957) — the THREADS-armed twin of the
 *   empty-lap cap, bound on the lap markers pushReworkChanges stamps per leg
 *   close ({head, pushed, resolved}): after this many consecutive laps on

 *   arm_rework action AND the restore_rework_arm sweep withhold the arm and
 *   escalate the owner once per head (label rework-loop-escalated + 🛑
 *   comment) instead of re-arming forever (live dart #424: 7 no-op legs / 2h
 *   starved the whole queue). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a
 *   new head, resets the budget by construction.
 *   jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs (default 45000, gh-848) — the
 *   twin-guard cancel polls a selected stale run until its jobs materialize

/**
 * Factory token usage — per-leg token-usage publisher (owner directive
 * 2026-10-13: factory glue moves into dmtools-agents as JS agent code; awf
 * workflows become thin callers).
 *
 * JS port of the awf factory-teammate.yml step «Publish leg token usage
 * (fa-tokens ledger -> factory-data)» — byte-extracted into
 * scripts/publish-token-usage.sh by IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows#34.
 * Behavior contract is identical:
 *
 *   1. Read the run output (RUN_OUTPUT). Missing/empty → skip (warn).
 *   2. Sum every `fa-tokens: {…}` ledger line (resume-aware: one line per
 *      session segment) — balanced-brace scan so a payload wrapped in a log
 *      line is found whole; invalid payloads are skipped. input/output/
 *      cacheRead are summed; the last-seen model wins. Zero in+out → skip.
 *   3. Leg: the run guard collapses the rework slot into kind="dev", so the
 *      true leg is recovered from the runner-config basename — *rework* →
 *      "rework", else KIND, else "dev".
 *   4. Anchor → key: pr-* passes through; gh-N → issue-N; anything else →
 *      skip (warn).
 *   5. Row (printf field order): {"leg","at","prompt","completion","total",
 *      "cacheRead","model"} — at = UTC ISO-8601 seconds.
 *   6. Bootstrap the factory-data branch from the default-branch head
 *      (422 "already exists" is the normal case), then up to 3 attempts:
 *      GET contents (sha + body), append the row under the key, drop rows
 *      older than 14 days, keep the last 40 per key, drop emptied keys,
 *      PUT Contents API with the existing sha. Conflict → refetch → retry
 *      (sh backoff attempt*2s). Exhausted → warn; rows are decorative and
 *      the next leg retries.
 *
 * Transport mirrors factoryState.js: every command starts with `gh` (the
 * executor whitelists the first token); base64 stays in-shell
 * (`printf %s … | base64` / `--jq .content | base64 -d`) so the JS side
 * never needs a base64 codec.
 *
 * Env/file contract (the sh step's env block; the JSRunner entry reads
 * jobParams.customParams first, these env names as fallback):
 *   RUN_OUTPUT   path of the captured run output (fa-tokens ledger source)
 *   CONFIG       runner config path; basename minus .json decides the leg
 *   KIND         leg kind when the basename has no "rework" (default "dev")
 *   ANCHOR       work anchor: pr-<n> | gh-<n>
 *   REPO         owner/repo of the factory-data target
 *   DATA_BRANCH  target branch (default "factory-data")
 *   DATA_PATH    target path   (default "data/fa-tokens.json")

 * Behavior contract is identical:
 *
 *   1. Read the run output (RUN_OUTPUT). Missing/empty → skip (warn).
 *   2. Sum every `fa-tokens: {…}` ledger line (resume-aware: one line per
 *      session segment) — balanced-brace scan so a payload wrapped in a log
 *      line is found whole; invalid payloads are skipped. input/output/
 *      cacheRead are summed; the last-seen model wins. Zero in+out → skip.
 *   3. Leg: the run guard collapses the rework slot into kind="dev", so the
 *      true leg is recovered from the runner-config basename — *rework* →

 *   4. Anchor → key: pr-* passes through; gh-N → issue-N; anything else →
 *      skip (warn).
 *   5. Row (printf field order): {"leg","at","prompt","completion","total",
 *      "cacheRead","model"} — at = UTC ISO-8601 seconds.
 *   6. Bootstrap the factory-data branch from the default-branch head
 *      (422 "already exists" is the normal case), then up to 3 attempts:
 *      GET contents (sha + body), append the row under the key, drop rows
 *      older than 14 days, keep the last 40 per key, drop emptied keys,
 *      PUT Contents API with the existing sha. Conflict → refetch → retry
 *      (sh backoff attempt*2s). Exhausted → warn; rows are decorative and
 *      the next leg retries.

/**
 * Factory token usage — per-leg token-usage publisher (owner directive
 * 2026-10-13: factory glue moves into dmtools-agents as JS agent code; awf
 * workflows become thin callers).
 *
 * JS port of the awf factory-teammate.yml step «Publish leg token usage
 * (fa-tokens ledger -> factory-data)» — byte-extracted into
 * scripts/publish-token-usage.sh by IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows#34.
 * Behavior contract is identical:
 *
 *   1. Read the run output (RUN_OUTPUT). Missing/empty → skip (warn).
 *   2. Sum every `fa-tokens: {…}` ledger line (resume-aware: one line per
 *      session segment) — balanced-brace scan so a payload wrapped in a log
 *      line is found whole; invalid payloads are skipped. input/output/
 *      cacheRead are summed; the last-seen model wins. Zero in+out → skip.
 *   3. Leg: the run guard collapses the rework slot into kind="dev", so the
 *      true leg is recovered from the runner-config basename — *rework* →
 *      "rework", else KIND, else "dev".
 *   4. Anchor → key: pr-* passes through; gh-N → issue-N; anything else →
 *      skip (warn).
 *   5. Row (printf field order): {"leg","at","prompt","completion","total",
 *      "cacheRead","model"} — at = UTC ISO-8601 seconds.
 *   6. Bootstrap the factory-data branch from the default-branch head
 *      (422 "already exists" is the normal case), then up to 3 attempts:
 *      GET contents (sha + body), append the row under the key, drop rows
 *      older than 14 days, keep the last 40 per key, drop emptied keys,
 *      PUT Contents API with the existing sha. Conflict → refetch → retry
 *      (sh backoff attempt*2s). Exhausted → warn; rows are decorative and
 *      the next leg retries.
 *
 * Transport mirrors factoryState.js: every command starts with `gh` (the
 * executor whitelists the first token); base64 stays in-shell
 * (`printf %s … | base64` / `--jq .content | base64 -d`) so the JS side
 * never needs a base64 codec.
 *
 * Env/file contract (the sh step's env block; the JSRunner entry reads
 * jobParams.customParams first, these env names as fallback):
 *   RUN_OUTPUT   path of the captured run output (fa-tokens ledger source)
 *   CONFIG       runner config path; basename minus .json decides the leg
 *   KIND         leg kind when the basename has no "rework" (default "dev")
 *   ANCHOR       work anchor: pr-<n> | gh-<n>
 *   REPO         owner/repo of the factory-data target
 *   DATA_BRANCH  target branch (default "factory-data")
 *   DATA_PATH    target path   (default "data/fa-tokens.json")
 *
 * Pure functions carry no IO: the publisher takes { exec, read, sleepMs,
 * log } capturers (factoryState.js convention) so tests mock the transport
 * via loadModule without touching any global.
 */

/**
 * Factory token usage — per-leg token-usage publisher (owner directive
 * 2026-10-13: factory glue moves into dmtools-agents as JS agent code; awf
 * workflows become thin callers).
 *
 * JS port of the awf factory-teammate.yml step «Publish leg token usage
 * (fa-tokens ledger -> factory-data)» — byte-extracted into
 * scripts/publish-token-usage.sh by IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows#34.
 * Behavior contract is identical:
 *
 *   1. Read the run output (RUN_OUTPUT). Missing/empty → skip (warn).
 *   2. Sum every `fa-tokens: {…}` ledger line (resume-aware: one line per
 *      session segment) — balanced-brace scan so a payload wrapped in a log
 *      line is found whole; invalid payloads are skipped. input/output/
 *      cacheRead are summed; the last-seen model wins. Zero in+out → skip.
 *   3. Leg: the run guard collapses the rework slot into kind="dev", so the
 *      true leg is recovered from the runner-config basename — *rework* →
 *      "rework", else KIND, else "dev".
 *   4. Anchor → key: pr-* passes through; gh-N → issue-N; anything else →
 *      skip (warn).
 *   5. Row (printf field order): {"leg","at","prompt","completion","total",
 *      "cacheRead","model"} — at = UTC ISO-8601 seconds.
 *   6. Bootstrap the factory-data branch from the default-branch head
 *      (422 "already exists" is the normal case), then up to 3 attempts:
 *      GET contents (sha + body), append the row under the key, drop rows
 *      older than 14 days, keep the last 40 per key, drop emptied keys,
 *      PUT Contents API with the existing sha. Conflict → refetch → retry
 *      (sh backoff attempt*2s). Exhausted → warn; rows are decorative and
 *      the next leg retries.
 *
 * Transport mirrors factoryState.js: every command starts with `gh` (the
 * executor whitelists the first token); base64 stays in-shell
 * (`printf %s … | base64` / `--jq .content | base64 -d`) so the JS side
 * never needs a base64 codec.
 *
 * Env/file contract (the sh step's env block; the JSRunner entry reads
 * jobParams.customParams first, these env names as fallback):
 *   RUN_OUTPUT   path of the captured run output (fa-tokens ledger source)
 *   CONFIG       runner config path; basename minus .json decides the leg
 *   KIND         leg kind when the basename has no "rework" (default "dev")
 *   ANCHOR       work anchor: pr-<n> | gh-<n>
 *   REPO         owner/repo of the factory-data target
 *   DATA_BRANCH  target branch (default "factory-data")
 *   DATA_PATH    target path   (default "data/fa-tokens.json")
 *
 * Pure functions carry no IO: the publisher takes { exec, read, sleepMs,
 * log } capturers (factoryState.js convention) so tests mock the transport
 * via loadModule without touching any global.

 * Runtime require model (verified empirically against the dmtools runtime

 *   - a require executed WHILE a module initializes (top level, top-level

/**
 * Unit tests for js/common/checkRunZombies.js — the gate-ghost classifier (gh-842).
 *
 * Bug (live fa #1457, 2026-10-10, head 7d00a1b2): a dispatched CI run was
 * CANCELLED while queued (gh-748 twin-guard family); the in_progress check
 * runs it registered on the head were never concluded. Branch protection
 * takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so the ghosts held
 * mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED for ~2h even though the head also carried GREEN
 * terminal entries from the earlier run 38057801418. The tick's green-cover
 * guard (skipIfGreenCi) read the green run as covering the head and never
 * re-dispatched — the gate idled until an operator nudged a fresh dispatch.
 *
 * Coverage (ticket test plan L1 — zombie classification):
 *   no-run           — in_progress check-run whose backing run no longer
 *                      exists (absent from the head's run list / 404)
 *   cancelled        — backing run concluded cancelled
 *   stale-no-runner  — no run link (bridge stamp) and older than the
 *                      stale threshold with no runner behind it
 *   run-concluded    — backing run concluded (non-cancelled) past the
 *                      propagation grace — the run ended, the check ghosted
 *   live (AC2)       — backing run ACTIVE, fresh stamp, propagation lag, or
 *                      probe error — a genuinely in-progress run is NEVER
 *                      disturbed; probe failures fail SAFE toward live
 *   settled checks   — concluded check-runs are not zombies (a green
 *                      terminal entry next to a ghost stays green evidence)
 *   #1457 replay     — the real timeline: 3 ghost contexts (run deleted)
 *                      + green terminal entries from the older run
 *
 * Pure module — no tool globals; loadModule with no mocks.
 */

/**

 * Bug (live fa #1457, 2026-10-10, head 7d00a1b2): a dispatched CI run was
 * CANCELLED while queued (gh-748 twin-guard family); the in_progress check
 * runs it registered on the head were never concluded. Branch protection
 * takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so the ghosts held
 * mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED for ~2h even though the head also carried GREEN
 * terminal entries from the earlier run 38057801418. The tick's green-cover
 * guard (skipIfGreenCi) read the green run as covering the head and never
 * re-dispatched — the gate idled until an operator nudged a fresh dispatch.
 *
 * Coverage (ticket test plan L1 — zombie classification):
 *   no-run           — in_progress check-run whose backing run no longer
 *                      exists (absent from the head's run list / 404)
 *   cancelled        — backing run concluded cancelled
 *   stale-no-runner  — no run link (bridge stamp) and older than the
 *                      stale threshold with no runner behind it
 *   run-concluded    — backing run concluded (non-cancelled) past the
 *                      propagation grace — the run ended, the check ghosted
 *   live (AC2)       — backing run ACTIVE, fresh stamp, propagation lag, or
 *                      probe error — a genuinely in-progress run is NEVER

/**
 * Unit tests for js/common/checkRunZombies.js — the gate-ghost classifier (gh-842).
 *
 * Bug (live fa #1457, 2026-10-10, head 7d00a1b2): a dispatched CI run was
 * CANCELLED while queued (gh-748 twin-guard family); the in_progress check
 * runs it registered on the head were never concluded. Branch protection
 * takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so the ghosts held
 * mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED for ~2h even though the head also carried GREEN
 * terminal entries from the earlier run 38057801418. The tick's green-cover
 * guard (skipIfGreenCi) read the green run as covering the head and never
 * re-dispatched — the gate idled until an operator nudged a fresh dispatch.
 *
 * Coverage (ticket test plan L1 — zombie classification):
 *   no-run           — in_progress check-run whose backing run no longer
 *                      exists (absent from the head's run list / 404)
 *   cancelled        — backing run concluded cancelled
 *   stale-no-runner  — no run link (bridge stamp) and older than the
 *                      stale threshold with no runner behind it
 *   run-concluded    — backing run concluded (non-cancelled) past the
 *                      propagation grace — the run ended, the check ghosted
 *   live (AC2)       — backing run ACTIVE, fresh stamp, propagation lag, or
 *                      probe error — a genuinely in-progress run is NEVER
 *                      disturbed; probe failures fail SAFE toward live
 *   settled checks   — concluded check-runs are not zombies (a green
 *                      terminal entry next to a ghost stays green evidence)
 *   #1457 replay     — the real timeline: 3 ghost contexts (run deleted)

/**
 * Factory token usage — per-leg token-usage publisher (owner directive
 * 2026-10-13: factory glue moves into dmtools-agents as JS agent code; awf
 * workflows become thin callers).
 *
 * JS port of the awf factory-teammate.yml step «Publish leg token usage
 * (fa-tokens ledger -> factory-data)» — byte-extracted into
 * scripts/publish-token-usage.sh by IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows#34.
 * Behavior contract is identical:
 *
 *   1. Read the run output (RUN_OUTPUT). Missing/empty → skip (warn).
 *   2. Sum every `fa-tokens: {…}` ledger line (resume-aware: one line per
 *      session segment) — balanced-brace scan so a payload wrapped in a log
 *      line is found whole; invalid payloads are skipped. input/output/
 *      cacheRead are summed; the last-seen model wins. Zero in+out → skip.
 *   3. Leg: the run guard collapses the rework slot into kind="dev", so the
 *      true leg is recovered from the runner-config basename — *rework* →
 *      "rework", else KIND, else "dev".
 *   4. Anchor → key: pr-* passes through; gh-N → issue-N; anything else →
 *      skip (warn).
 *   5. Row (printf field order): {"leg","at","prompt","completion","total",
 *      "cacheRead","model"} — at = UTC ISO-8601 seconds.
 *   6. Bootstrap the factory-data branch from the default-branch head
 *      (422 "already exists" is the normal case), then up to 3 attempts:
 *      GET contents (sha + body), append the row under the key, drop rows
 *      older than 14 days, keep the last 40 per key, drop emptied keys,
 *      PUT Contents API with the existing sha. Conflict → refetch → retry
 *      (sh backoff attempt*2s). Exhausted → warn; rows are decorative and
 *      the next leg retries.

/**
 * Factory token usage — per-leg token-usage publisher (owner directive
 * 2026-10-13: factory glue moves into dmtools-agents as JS agent code; awf
 * workflows become thin callers).

 * JS port of the awf factory-teammate.yml step «Publish leg token usage
 * (fa-tokens ledger -> factory-data)» — byte-extracted into
 * scripts/publish-token-usage.sh by IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows#34.
 * Behavior contract is identical:
 *
 *   1. Read the run output (RUN_OUTPUT). Missing/empty → skip (warn).
 *   2. Sum every `fa-tokens: {…}` ledger line (resume-aware: one line per
 *      session segment) — balanced-brace scan so a payload wrapped in a log
 *      line is found whole; invalid payloads are skipped. input/output/
 *      cacheRead are summed; the last-seen model wins. Zero in+out → skip.
 *   3. Leg: the run guard collapses the rework slot into kind="dev", so the
 *      true leg is recovered from the runner-config basename — *rework* →
 *      "rework", else KIND, else "dev".
 *   4. Anchor → key: pr-* passes through; gh-N → issue-N; anything else →
 *      skip (warn).
 *   5. Row (printf field order): {"leg","at","prompt","completion","total",
 *      "cacheRead","model"} — at = UTC ISO-8601 seconds.
 *   6. Bootstrap the factory-data branch from the default-branch head
 *      (422 "already exists" is the normal case), then up to 3 attempts:
 *      GET contents (sha + body), append the row under the key, drop rows
 *      older than 14 days, keep the last 40 per key, drop emptied keys,
 *      PUT Contents API with the existing sha. Conflict → refetch → retry
 *      (sh backoff attempt*2s). Exhausted → warn; rows are decorative and
 *      the next leg retries.
 *
 * Transport mirrors factoryState.js: every command starts with `gh` (the
 * executor whitelists the first token); base64 stays in-shell
 * (`printf %s … | base64` / `--jq .content | base64 -d`) so the JS side
 * never needs a base64 codec.
 *
 * Env/file contract (the sh step's env block; the JSRunner entry reads
 * jobParams.customParams first, these env names as fallback):
 *   RUN_OUTPUT   path of the captured run output (fa-tokens ledger source)
 *   CONFIG       runner config path; basename minus .json decides the leg
 *   KIND         leg kind when the basename has no "rework" (default "dev")
 *   ANCHOR       work anchor: pr-<n> | gh-<n>
 *   REPO         owner/repo of the factory-data target
 *   DATA_BRANCH  target branch (default "factory-data")
 *   DATA_PATH    target path   (default "data/fa-tokens.json")
 *
 * Pure functions carry no IO: the publisher takes { exec, read, sleepMs,
 * log } capturers (factoryState.js convention) so tests mock the transport

/**

 * Bug (live fa #1457, 2026-10-10, head 7d00a1b2): a dispatched CI run was

 * runs it registered on the head were never concluded. Branch protection
 * takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so the ghosts held

 * guard (skipIfGreenCi) read the green run as covering the head and never
 * re-dispatched — the gate idled until an operator nudged a fresh dispatch.

 * Coverage (ticket test plan L1 — zombie classification):
 *   no-run           — in_progress check-run whose backing run no longer
 *                      exists (absent from the head's run list / 404)
 *   cancelled        — backing run concluded cancelled
 *   stale-no-runner  — no run link (bridge stamp) and older than the
 *                      stale threshold with no runner behind it
 *   run-concluded    — backing run concluded (non-cancelled) past the
 *                      propagation grace — the run ended, the check ghosted
 *   live (AC2)       — backing run ACTIVE, fresh stamp, propagation lag, or
 *                      probe error — a genuinely in-progress run is NEVER
 *                      disturbed; probe failures fail SAFE toward live
 *   settled checks   — concluded check-runs are not zombies (a green
 *                      terminal entry next to a ghost stays green evidence)
 *   #1457 replay     — the real timeline: 3 ghost contexts (run deleted)

/**

 * Bug (live fa #1457, 2026-10-10, head 7d00a1b2): a dispatched CI run was

 * runs it registered on the head were never concluded. Branch protection
 * takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so the ghosts held
 * mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED for ~2h even though the head also carried GREEN
 * terminal entries from the earlier run 38057801418. The tick's green-cover
 * guard (skipIfGreenCi) read the green run as covering the head and never
 * re-dispatched — the gate idled until an operator nudged a fresh dispatch.
 *
 * Coverage (ticket test plan L1 — zombie classification):
 *   no-run           — in_progress check-run whose backing run no longer
 *                      exists (absent from the head's run list / 404)
 *   cancelled        — backing run concluded cancelled
 *   stale-no-runner  — no run link (bridge stamp) and older than the
 *                      stale threshold with no runner behind it
 *   run-concluded    — backing run concluded (non-cancelled) past the
 *                      propagation grace — the run ended, the check ghosted
 *   live (AC2)       — backing run ACTIVE, fresh stamp, propagation lag, or
 *                      probe error — a genuinely in-progress run is NEVER
 *                      disturbed; probe failures fail SAFE toward live
 *   settled checks   — concluded check-runs are not zombies (a green
 *                      terminal entry next to a ghost stays green evidence)
 *   #1457 replay     — the real timeline: 3 ghost contexts (run deleted)

 * Pure module — no tool globals; loadModule with no mocks.

 * runs it registered on the head were never concluded. Branch protection
 * takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so the ghosts held
 * mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED for ~2h even though the head also carried GREEN
 * terminal entries from the earlier run 38057801418. The tick's green-cover
 * guard (skipIfGreenCi) read the green run as covering the head and never
 * re-dispatched — the gate idled until an operator nudged a fresh dispatch.
 *
 * Coverage (ticket test plan L1 — zombie classification):
 *   no-run           — in_progress check-run whose backing run no longer
 *                      exists (absent from the head's run list / 404)
 *   cancelled        — backing run concluded cancelled
 *   stale-no-runner  — no run link (bridge stamp) and older than the
 *                      stale threshold with no runner behind it
 *   run-concluded    — backing run concluded (non-cancelled) past the
 *                      propagation grace — the run ended, the check ghosted
 *   live (AC2)       — backing run ACTIVE, fresh stamp, propagation lag, or
 *                      probe error — a genuinely in-progress run is NEVER
 *                      disturbed; probe failures fail SAFE toward live
 *   settled checks   — concluded check-runs are not zombies (a green
 *                      terminal entry next to a ghost stays green evidence)

/**
 * Unit tests for js/common/checkRunZombies.js — the gate-ghost classifier (gh-842).
 *
 * Bug (live fa #1457, 2026-10-10, head 7d00a1b2): a dispatched CI run was
 * CANCELLED while queued (gh-748 twin-guard family); the in_progress check
 * runs it registered on the head were never concluded. Branch protection
 * takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so the ghosts held
 * mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED for ~2h even though the head also carried GREEN
 * terminal entries from the earlier run 38057801418. The tick's green-cover
 * guard (skipIfGreenCi) read the green run as covering the head and never
 * re-dispatched — the gate idled until an operator nudged a fresh dispatch.
 *
 * Coverage (ticket test plan L1 — zombie classification):
 *   no-run           — in_progress check-run whose backing run no longer
 *                      exists (absent from the head's run list / 404)
 *   cancelled        — backing run concluded cancelled
 *   stale-no-runner  — no run link (bridge stamp) and older than the
 *                      stale threshold with no runner behind it
 *   run-concluded    — backing run concluded (non-cancelled) past the
 *                      propagation grace — the run ended, the check ghosted
 *   live (AC2)       — backing run ACTIVE, fresh stamp, propagation lag, or
 *                      probe error — a genuinely in-progress run is NEVER
 *                      disturbed; probe failures fail SAFE toward live
 *   settled checks   — concluded check-runs are not zombies (a green
 *                      terminal entry next to a ghost stays green evidence)
 *   #1457 replay     — the real timeline: 3 ghost contexts (run deleted)
 *                      + green terminal entries from the older run
 *
 * Pure module — no tool globals; loadModule with no mocks.
 */

/**
 * Unit tests for js/common/checkRunZombies.js — the gate-ghost classifier (gh-842).
 *
 * Bug (live fa #1457, 2026-10-10, head 7d00a1b2): a dispatched CI run was
 * CANCELLED while queued (gh-748 twin-guard family); the in_progress check
 * runs it registered on the head were never concluded. Branch protection
 * takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so the ghosts held
 * mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED for ~2h even though the head also carried GREEN
 * terminal entries from the earlier run 38057801418. The tick's green-cover
 * guard (skipIfGreenCi) read the green run as covering the head and never
 * re-dispatched — the gate idled until an operator nudged a fresh dispatch.
 *
 * Coverage (ticket test plan L1 — zombie classification):
 *   no-run           — in_progress check-run whose backing run no longer
 *                      exists (absent from the head's run list / 404)
 *   cancelled        — backing run concluded cancelled
 *   stale-no-runner  — no run link (bridge stamp) and older than the
 *                      stale threshold with no runner behind it
 *   run-concluded    — backing run concluded (non-cancelled) past the
 *                      propagation grace — the run ended, the check ghosted
 *   live (AC2)       — backing run ACTIVE, fresh stamp, propagation lag, or
 *                      probe error — a genuinely in-progress run is NEVER
 *                      disturbed; probe failures fail SAFE toward live
 *   settled checks   — concluded check-runs are not zombies (a green
 *                      terminal entry next to a ghost stays green evidence)
 *   #1457 replay     — the real timeline: 3 ghost contexts (run deleted)
 *                      + green terminal entries from the older run
 *
 * Pure module — no tool globals; loadModule with no mocks.
 */

/**

 * Bug (live fa #1457, 2026-10-10, head 7d00a1b2): a dispatched CI run was
 * CANCELLED while queued (gh-748 twin-guard family); the in_progress check
 * runs it registered on the head were never concluded. Branch protection
 * takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so the ghosts held
 * mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED for ~2h even though the head also carried GREEN
 * terminal entries from the earlier run 38057801418. The tick's green-cover
 * guard (skipIfGreenCi) read the green run as covering the head and never
 * re-dispatched — the gate idled until an operator nudged a fresh dispatch.
 *
 * Coverage (ticket test plan L1 — zombie classification):
 *   no-run           — in_progress check-run whose backing run no longer
 *                      exists (absent from the head's run list / 404)
 *   cancelled        — backing run concluded cancelled
 *   stale-no-runner  — no run link (bridge stamp) and older than the
 *                      stale threshold with no runner behind it
 *   run-concluded    — backing run concluded (non-cancelled) past the
 *                      propagation grace — the run ended, the check ghosted
 *   live (AC2)       — backing run ACTIVE, fresh stamp, propagation lag, or
 *                      probe error — a genuinely in-progress run is NEVER
 *                      disturbed; probe failures fail SAFE toward live
 *   settled checks   — concluded check-runs are not zombies (a green
 *                      terminal entry next to a ghost stays green evidence)
 *   #1457 replay     — the real timeline: 3 ghost contexts (run deleted)

 * Pure module — no tool globals; loadModule with no mocks.
 */

/**

/**
 * Unit tests for js/common/checkRunZombies.js — the gate-ghost classifier (gh-842).

 * Bug (live fa #1457, 2026-10-10, head 7d00a1b2): a dispatched CI run was
 * CANCELLED while queued (gh-748 twin-guard family); the in_progress check
 * runs it registered on the head were never concluded. Branch protection
 * takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so the ghosts held
 * mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED for ~2h even though the head also carried GREEN
 * terminal entries from the earlier run 38057801418. The tick's green-cover
 * guard (skipIfGreenCi) read the green run as covering the head and never
 * re-dispatched — the gate idled until an operator nudged a fresh dispatch.
 *
 * Coverage (ticket test plan L1 — zombie classification):
 *   no-run           — in_progress check-run whose backing run no longer
 *                      exists (absent from the head's run list / 404)
 *   cancelled        — backing run concluded cancelled
 *   stale-no-runner  — no run link (bridge stamp) and older than the
 *                      stale threshold with no runner behind it
 *   run-concluded    — backing run concluded (non-cancelled) past the
 *                      propagation grace — the run ended, the check ghosted
 *   live (AC2)       — backing run ACTIVE, fresh stamp, propagation lag, or
 *                      probe error — a genuinely in-progress run is NEVER
 *                      disturbed; probe failures fail SAFE toward live
 *   settled checks   — concluded check-runs are not zombies (a green
 *                      terminal entry next to a ghost stays green evidence)

blocks.text: I made a mess with these regex edits — `')` became `'', function`. Let me just rewrite the suite header lines cleanly with a script that normalizes: `suite('NAME');` → `suite('NAME', function () {` and adds `});` at each suite's end. Simpler: rewrite the whole test file with proper structure from scratch (I have the content). Cleaner than patching.
Let me just rewrite the test file cleanly:

{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'
import re
p = 'js/unit-tests/test_checkRunStamp.js'
src = open(p).read()
src = src.replace("'', function () {", "', function () {")
# find suite header lines and inject closing '});' before the NEXT suite header or EOF
lines = src.split('\n')
out = []
suite_idxs = [i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if l.startswith("suite('")]
for i, l in enumerate(lines):
    out.append(l)
    if i in suite_idxs:
        continue
# simpler: rebuild — after each suite header, tests follow until next suite header; append '});' before next header
out = []
for i, l in enumerate(lines):
    if i in suite_idxs and i > suite_idxs[0]:
        out.append('});')
        out.append('')
    out.append(l)
out.append('});')
src = '\n'.join(out)
open(p, 'w').write(src)
EOF

/**
 * Unit tests for js/common/checkRunZombies.js — the gate-ghost classifier (gh-842).
 *
 * Bug (live fa #1457, 2026-10-10, head 7d00a1b2): a dispatched CI run was
 * CANCELLED while queued (gh-748 twin-guard family); the in_progress check
 * runs it registered on the head were never concluded. Branch protection
 * takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so the ghosts held
 * mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED for ~2h even though the head also carried GREEN
 * terminal entries from the earlier run 38057801418. The tick's green-cover
 * guard (skipIfGreenCi) read the green run as covering the head and never
 * re-dispatched — the gate idled until an operator nudged a fresh dispatch.
 *
 * Coverage (ticket test plan L1 — zombie classification):
 *   no-run           — in_progress check-run whose backing run no longer
 *                      exists (absent from the head's run list / 404)
 *   cancelled        — backing run concluded cancelled
 *   stale-no-runner  — no run link (bridge stamp) and older than the
 *                      stale threshold with no runner behind it
 *   run-concluded    — backing run concluded (non-cancelled) past the
 *                      propagation grace — the run ended, the check ghosted
 *   live (AC2)       — backing run ACTIVE, fresh stamp, propagation lag, or
 *                      probe error — a genuinely in-progress run is NEVER
 *                      disturbed; probe failures fail SAFE toward live
 *   settled checks   — concluded check-runs are not zombies (a green
 *                      terminal entry next to a ghost stays green evidence)
 *   #1457 replay     — the real timeline: 3 ghost contexts (run deleted)
 *                      + green terminal entries from the older run
 *
 * Pure module — no tool globals; loadModule with no mocks.
 */

/**
 * Unit tests for js/common/checkRunZombies.js — the gate-ghost classifier (gh-842).
 *
 * Bug (live fa #1457, 2026-10-10, head 7d00a1b2): a dispatched CI run was
 * CANCELLED while queued (gh-748 twin-guard family); the in_progress check
 * runs it registered on the head were never concluded. Branch protection
 * takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so the ghosts held
 * mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED for ~2h even though the head also carried GREEN
 * terminal entries from the earlier run 38057801418. The tick's green-cover
 * guard (skipIfGreenCi) read the green run as covering the head and never
 * re-dispatched — the gate idled until an operator nudged a fresh dispatch.
 *
 * Coverage (ticket test plan L1 — zombie classification):
 *   no-run           — in_progress check-run whose backing run no longer
 *                      exists (absent from the head's run list / 404)
 *   cancelled        — backing run concluded cancelled
 *   stale-no-runner  — no run link (bridge stamp) and older than the
 *                      stale threshold with no runner behind it
 *   run-concluded    — backing run concluded (non-cancelled) past the
 *                      propagation grace — the run ended, the check ghosted
 *   live (AC2)       — backing run ACTIVE, fresh stamp, propagation lag, or
 *                      probe error — a genuinely in-progress run is NEVER
 *                      disturbed; probe failures fail SAFE toward live
 *   settled checks   — concluded check-runs are not zombies (a green
 *                      terminal entry next to a ghost stays green evidence)
 *   #1457 replay     — the real timeline: 3 ghost contexts (run deleted)
 *                      + green terminal entries from the older run
 *
 * Pure module — no tool globals; loadModule with no mocks.
 */

/**
 * Unit tests for js/common/checkRunZombies.js — the gate-ghost classifier (gh-842).
 *
 * Bug (live fa #1457, 2026-10-10, head 7d00a1b2): a dispatched CI run was
 * CANCELLED while queued (gh-748 twin-guard family); the in_progress check
 * runs it registered on the head were never concluded. Branch protection
 * takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so the ghosts held
 * mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED for ~2h even though the head also carried GREEN
 * terminal entries from the earlier run 38057801418. The tick's green-cover
 * guard (skipIfGreenCi) read the green run as covering the head and never
 * re-dispatched — the gate idled until an operator nudged a fresh dispatch.
 *
 * Coverage (ticket test plan L1 — zombie classification):
 *   no-run           — in_progress check-run whose backing run no longer
 *                      exists (absent from the head's run list / 404)
 *   cancelled        — backing run concluded cancelled
 *   stale-no-runner  — no run link (bridge stamp) and older than the
 *                      stale threshold with no runner behind it
 *   run-concluded    — backing run concluded (non-cancelled) past the
 *                      propagation grace — the run ended, the check ghosted
 *   live (AC2)       — backing run ACTIVE, fresh stamp, propagation lag, or
 *                      probe error — a genuinely in-progress run is NEVER
 *                      disturbed; probe failures fail SAFE toward live
 *   settled checks   — concluded check-runs are not zombies (a green
 *                      terminal entry next to a ghost stays green evidence)
 *   #1457 replay     — the real timeline: 3 ghost contexts (run deleted)
 *                      + green terminal entries from the older run
 *
 * Pure module — no tool globals; loadModule with no mocks.
 */

'use strict';
/**
 * Pack-release require sanity gate (gh-812, live incident 2026-10-09).
 *
 * The release self-test demanded by gh-812 AC1/AC3: after a pack zip is
 * built, every literal relative `require('./x')` / `require('../y')` in
 * every packed .js must resolve to a file INSIDE the zip — a pack whose
 * code requires a module the zip does not carry must FAIL the release
 * (exit != 0) before the ledger commit and the publish, not live on the
 * fa runners ("Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js").
 *
 * validatePack() cannot catch this class: it re-hashes manifest entries
 * against themselves, which proves the zip matches its manifest, never
 * that the payload is self-consistent.
 *
 * Pure classification — no fs, no zip, no exec: the caller (ci/release_packs.mjs)
 * extracts the zip and hands over {path, source} records; this CommonJS twin
 * of the builder keeps the decisions unit-testable in the dmtools runner
 * (same split as ci/pack_release_guard.cjs).
 *
 * Known limit (documented, gh-812 test plan): dynamically assembled requires
 * (`require(prefix + name + '.js')`) cannot be resolved statically and are
 * ignored. The require that broke the incident was a string literal, and
 * every require in this repo's packed code is. Comment/JSdoc text is NOT
 * stripped — the runtime resolver union (see resolveRequireCandidates) kept
 * every doc example in this repo resolvable, and stripping risks missing a
 * real require swallowed by a misdetected regex literal.
 */

/** Literal relative require: require('./a.js'), require ("../b/c.js"). */

'use strict';
/**
 * Pack-release require sanity gate (gh-812, live incident 2026-10-09).
 *
 * The release self-test demanded by gh-812 AC1/AC3: after a pack zip is
 * built, every literal relative `require('./x')` / `require('../y')` in
 * every packed .js must resolve to a file INSIDE the zip — a pack whose
 * code requires a module the zip does not carry must FAIL the release
 * (exit != 0) before the ledger commit and the publish, not live on the
 * fa runners ("Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js").
 *
 * validatePack() cannot catch this class: it re-hashes manifest entries
 * against themselves, which proves the zip matches its manifest, never
 * that the payload is self-consistent.
 *
 * Pure classification — no fs, no zip, no exec: the caller (ci/release_packs.mjs)
 * extracts the zip and hands over {path, source} records; this CommonJS twin
 * of the builder keeps the decisions unit-testable in the dmtools runner
 * (same split as ci/pack_release_guard.cjs).
 *
 * Known limit (documented, gh-812 test plan): dynamically assembled requires
 * (`require(prefix + name + '.js')`) cannot be resolved statically and are
 * ignored. The require that broke the incident was a string literal, and
 * every require in this repo's packed code is. Comment/JSdoc text is NOT
 * stripped — the runtime resolver union (see resolveRequireCandidates) kept
 * every doc example in this repo resolvable, and stripping risks missing a
 * real require swallowed by a misdetected regex literal.
 */

/** Literal relative require: require('./a.js'), require ("../b/c.js"). */

'use strict';
/**
 * Pack-release require sanity gate (gh-812, live incident 2026-10-09).
 *
 * The release self-test demanded by gh-812 AC1/AC3: after a pack zip is
 * built, every literal relative `require('./x')` / `require('../y')` in
 * every packed .js must resolve to a file INSIDE the zip — a pack whose
 * code requires a module the zip does not carry must FAIL the release
 * (exit != 0) before the ledger commit and the publish, not live on the
 * fa runners ("Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js").
 *
 * validatePack() cannot catch this class: it re-hashes manifest entries
 * against themselves, which proves the zip matches its manifest, never
 * that the payload is self-consistent.
 *
 * Pure classification — no fs, no zip, no exec: the caller (ci/release_packs.mjs)
 * extracts the zip and hands over {path, source} records; this CommonJS twin
 * of the builder keeps the decisions unit-testable in the dmtools runner
 * (same split as ci/pack_release_guard.cjs).
 *
 * Known limit (documented, gh-812 test plan): dynamically assembled requires
 * (`require(prefix + name + '.js')`) cannot be resolved statically and are
 * ignored. The require that broke the incident was a string literal, and
 * every require in this repo's packed code is. Comment/JSdoc text is NOT
 * stripped — the runtime resolver union (see resolveRequireCandidates) kept
 * every doc example in this repo resolvable, and stripping risks missing a
 * real require swallowed by a misdetected regex literal.
 */

/** Literal relative require: require('./a.js'), require ("../b/c.js"). */

'use strict';
/**
 * Pack-release require sanity gate (gh-812, live incident 2026-10-09).
 *
 * The release self-test demanded by gh-812 AC1/AC3: after a pack zip is
 * built, every literal relative `require('./x')` / `require('../y')` in
 * every packed .js must resolve to a file INSIDE the zip — a pack whose
 * code requires a module the zip does not carry must FAIL the release
 * (exit != 0) before the ledger commit and the publish, not live on the
 * fa runners ("Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js").
 *
 * validatePack() cannot catch this class: it re-hashes manifest entries
 * against themselves, which proves the zip matches its manifest, never
 * that the payload is self-consistent.
 *
 * Pure classification — no fs, no zip, no exec: the caller (ci/release_packs.mjs)
 * extracts the zip and hands over {path, source} records; this CommonJS twin
 * of the builder keeps the decisions unit-testable in the dmtools runner
 * (same split as ci/pack_release_guard.cjs).
 *
 * Known limit (documented, gh-812 test plan): dynamically assembled requires
 * (`require(prefix + name + '.js')`) cannot be resolved statically and are
 * ignored. The require that broke the incident was a string literal, and
 * every require in this repo's packed code is. Comment/JSdoc text is NOT
 * stripped — the runtime resolver union (see resolveRequireCandidates) kept
 * every doc example in this repo resolvable, and stripping risks missing a
 * real require swallowed by a misdetected regex literal.
 */

/** Literal relative require: require('./a.js'), require ("../b/c.js"). */

'use strict';
/**
 * Pack-release require sanity gate (gh-812, live incident 2026-10-09).
 *
 * The release self-test demanded by gh-812 AC1/AC3: after a pack zip is
 * built, every literal relative `require('./x')` / `require('../y')` in
 * every packed .js must resolve to a file INSIDE the zip — a pack whose
 * code requires a module the zip does not carry must FAIL the release
 * (exit != 0) before the ledger commit and the publish, not live on the
 * fa runners ("Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js").
 *
 * validatePack() cannot catch this class: it re-hashes manifest entries
 * against themselves, which proves the zip matches its manifest, never
 * that the payload is self-consistent.
 *
 * Pure classification — no fs, no zip, no exec: the caller (ci/release_packs.mjs)
 * extracts the zip and hands over {path, source} records; this CommonJS twin
 * of the builder keeps the decisions unit-testable in the dmtools runner
 * (same split as ci/pack_release_guard.cjs).
 *
 * Known limit (documented, gh-812 test plan): dynamically assembled requires
 * (`require(prefix + name + '.js')`) cannot be resolved statically and are
 * ignored. The require that broke the incident was a string literal, and
 * every require in this repo's packed code is. Comment/JSdoc text is NOT
 * stripped — the runtime resolver union (see resolveRequireCandidates) kept
 * every doc example in this repo resolvable, and stripping risks missing a
 * real require swallowed by a misdetected regex literal.
 */

/** Literal relative require: require('./a.js'), require ("../b/c.js"). */

'use strict';
/**
 * Pack-release require sanity gate (gh-812, live incident 2026-10-09).
 *
 * The release self-test demanded by gh-812 AC1/AC3: after a pack zip is
 * built, every literal relative `require('./x')` / `require('../y')` in
 * every packed .js must resolve to a file INSIDE the zip — a pack whose
 * code requires a module the zip does not carry must FAIL the release
 * (exit != 0) before the ledger commit and the publish, not live on the
 * fa runners ("Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js").
 *
 * validatePack() cannot catch this class: it re-hashes manifest entries
 * against themselves, which proves the zip matches its manifest, never
 * that the payload is self-consistent.
 *
 * Pure classification — no fs, no zip, no exec: the caller (ci/release_packs.mjs)
 * extracts the zip and hands over {path, source} records; this CommonJS twin
 * of the builder keeps the decisions unit-testable in the dmtools runner
 * (same split as ci/pack_release_guard.cjs).
 *
 * Known limit (documented, gh-812 test plan): dynamically assembled requires
 * (`require(prefix + name + '.js')`) cannot be resolved statically and are
 * ignored. The require that broke the incident was a string literal, and
 * every require in this repo's packed code is. Comment/JSdoc text is NOT
 * stripped — the runtime resolver union (see resolveRequireCandidates) kept
 * every doc example in this repo resolvable, and stripping risks missing a
 * real require swallowed by a misdetected regex literal.
 */

/** Literal relative require: require('./a.js'), require ("../b/c.js"). */

/**

 * The release self-test demanded by gh-812 AC1/AC3: after a pack zip is
 * built, every literal relative `require('./x')` / `require('../y')` in
 * every packed .js must resolve to a file INSIDE the zip — a pack whose
 * code requires a module the zip does not carry must FAIL the release
 * (exit != 0) before the ledger commit and the publish, not live on the
 * fa runners ("Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js").
 *
 * validatePack() cannot catch this class: it re-hashes manifest entries
 * against themselves, which proves the zip matches its manifest, never
 * that the payload is self-consistent.
 *
 * Pure classification — no fs, no zip, no exec: the caller (ci/release_packs.mjs)
 * extracts the zip and hands over {path, source} records; this CommonJS twin
 * of the builder keeps the decisions unit-testable in the dmtools runner
 * (same split as ci/pack_release_guard.cjs).
 *
 * Known limit (documented, gh-812 test plan): dynamically assembled requires
 * (`require(prefix + name + '.js')`) cannot be resolved statically and are
 * ignored. The require that broke the incident was a string literal, and
 * every require in this repo's packed code is. Comment/JSdoc text is NOT
 * stripped — the runtime resolver union (see resolveRequireCandidates) kept
 * every doc example in this repo resolvable, and stripping risks missing a
 * real require swallowed by a misdetected regex literal.
 */

'use strict';
/**
 * Pack-release require sanity gate (gh-812, live incident 2026-10-09).
 *
 * The release self-test demanded by gh-812 AC1/AC3: after a pack zip is
 * built, every literal relative `require('./x')` / `require('../y')` in
 * every packed .js must resolve to a file INSIDE the zip — a pack whose
 * code requires a module the zip does not carry must FAIL the release
 * (exit != 0) before the ledger commit and the publish, not live on the
 * fa runners ("Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js").
 *
 * validatePack() cannot catch this class: it re-hashes manifest entries
 * against themselves, which proves the zip matches its manifest, never
 * that the payload is self-consistent.
 *
 * Pure classification — no fs, no zip, no exec: the caller (ci/release_packs.mjs)
 * extracts the zip and hands over {path, source} records; this CommonJS twin
 * of the builder keeps the decisions unit-testable in the dmtools runner
 * (same split as ci/pack_release_guard.cjs).
 *
 * Known limit (documented, gh-812 test plan): dynamically assembled requires
 * (`require(prefix + name + '.js')`) cannot be resolved statically and are
 * ignored. The require that broke the incident was a string literal, and
 * every require in this repo's packed code is. Comment/JSdoc text is NOT
 * stripped — the runtime resolver union (see resolveRequireCandidates) kept
 * every doc example in this repo resolvable, and stripping risks missing a
 * real require swallowed by a misdetected regex literal.
 */

/** Literal relative require: require('./a.js'), require ("../b/c.js"). */

'use strict';
/**
 * Pack-release require sanity gate (gh-812, live incident 2026-10-09).
 *
 * The release self-test demanded by gh-812 AC1/AC3: after a pack zip is
 * built, every literal relative `require('./x')` / `require('../y')` in
 * every packed .js must resolve to a file INSIDE the zip — a pack whose
 * code requires a module the zip does not carry must FAIL the release
 * (exit != 0) before the ledger commit and the publish, not live on the
 * fa runners ("Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js").
 *
 * validatePack() cannot catch this class: it re-hashes manifest entries
 * against themselves, which proves the zip matches its manifest, never
 * that the payload is self-consistent.
 *
 * Pure classification — no fs, no zip, no exec: the caller (ci/release_packs.mjs)
 * extracts the zip and hands over {path, source} records; this CommonJS twin
 * of the builder keeps the decisions unit-testable in the dmtools runner
 * (same split as ci/pack_release_guard.cjs).
 *
 * Known limit (documented, gh-812 test plan): dynamically assembled requires
 * (`require(prefix + name + '.js')`) cannot be resolved statically and are
 * ignored. The require that broke the incident was a string literal, and
 * every require in this repo's packed code is. Comment/JSdoc text is NOT
 * stripped — the runtime resolver union (see resolveRequireCandidates) kept
 * every doc example in this repo resolvable, and stripping risks missing a
 * real require swallowed by a misdetected regex literal.
 */

/** Literal relative require: require('./a.js'), require ("../b/c.js"). */

 * every packed .js must resolve to a file INSIDE the zip — a pack whose

 * fa runners ("Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js").

 * validatePack() cannot catch this class: it re-hashes manifest entries
 * against themselves, which proves the zip matches its manifest, never
 * that the payload is self-consistent.
 *
 * Pure classification — no fs, no zip, no exec: the caller (ci/release_packs.mjs)
 * extracts the zip and hands over {path, source} records; this CommonJS twin
 * of the builder keeps the decisions unit-testable in the dmtools runner
 * (same split as ci/pack_release_guard.cjs).
 *
 * Known limit (documented, gh-812 test plan): dynamically assembled requires
 * (`require(prefix + name + '.js')`) cannot be resolved statically and are
 * ignored. The require that broke the incident was a string literal, and
 * every require in this repo's packed code is. Comment/JSdoc text is NOT
 * stripped — the runtime resolver union (see resolveRequireCandidates) kept
 * every doc example in this repo resolvable, and stripping risks missing a
 * real require swallowed by a misdetected regex literal.

'use strict';
/**
 * Pack-release require sanity gate (gh-812, live incident 2026-10-09).
 *
 * The release self-test demanded by gh-812 AC1/AC3: after a pack zip is
 * built, every literal relative `require('./x')` / `require('../y')` in
 * every packed .js must resolve to a file INSIDE the zip — a pack whose
 * code requires a module the zip does not carry must FAIL the release
 * (exit != 0) before the ledger commit and the publish, not live on the
 * fa runners ("Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js").
 *
 * validatePack() cannot catch this class: it re-hashes manifest entries
 * against themselves, which proves the zip matches its manifest, never
 * that the payload is self-consistent.
 *
 * Pure classification — no fs, no zip, no exec: the caller (ci/release_packs.mjs)
 * extracts the zip and hands over {path, source} records; this CommonJS twin
 * of the builder keeps the decisions unit-testable in the dmtools runner
 * (same split as ci/pack_release_guard.cjs).
 *
 * Known limit (documented, gh-812 test plan): dynamically assembled requires
 * (`require(prefix + name + '.js')`) cannot be resolved statically and are
 * ignored. The require that broke the incident was a string literal, and
 * every require in this repo's packed code is. Comment/JSdoc text is NOT
 * stripped — the runtime resolver union (see resolveRequireCandidates) kept
 * every doc example in this repo resolvable, and stripping risks missing a
 * real require swallowed by a misdetected regex literal.
 */

/** Literal relative require: require('./a.js'), require ("../b/c.js"). */

'use strict';
/**
 * Pack-release require sanity gate (gh-812, live incident 2026-10-09).
 *
 * The release self-test demanded by gh-812 AC1/AC3: after a pack zip is
 * built, every literal relative `require('./x')` / `require('../y')` in
 * every packed .js must resolve to a file INSIDE the zip — a pack whose
 * code requires a module the zip does not carry must FAIL the release
 * (exit != 0) before the ledger commit and the publish, not live on the
 * fa runners ("Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js").
 *
 * validatePack() cannot catch this class: it re-hashes manifest entries
 * against themselves, which proves the zip matches its manifest, never
 * that the payload is self-consistent.
 *
 * Pure classification — no fs, no zip, no exec: the caller (ci/release_packs.mjs)
 * extracts the zip and hands over {path, source} records; this CommonJS twin
 * of the builder keeps the decisions unit-testable in the dmtools runner
 * (same split as ci/pack_release_guard.cjs).
 *
 * Known limit (documented, gh-812 test plan): dynamically assembled requires
 * (`require(prefix + name + '.js')`) cannot be resolved statically and are
 * ignored. The require that broke the incident was a string literal, and
 * every require in this repo's packed code is. Comment/JSdoc text is NOT
 * stripped — the runtime resolver union (see resolveRequireCandidates) kept
 * every doc example in this repo resolvable, and stripping risks missing a
 * real require swallowed by a misdetected regex literal.
 */

/** Literal relative require: require('./a.js'), require ("../b/c.js"). */

'use strict';
/**
 * Pack-release require sanity gate (gh-812, live incident 2026-10-09).
 *
 * The release self-test demanded by gh-812 AC1/AC3: after a pack zip is
 * built, every literal relative `require('./x')` / `require('../y')` in
 * every packed .js must resolve to a file INSIDE the zip — a pack whose
 * code requires a module the zip does not carry must FAIL the release
 * (exit != 0) before the ledger commit and the publish, not live on the
 * fa runners ("Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js").
 *
 * validatePack() cannot catch this class: it re-hashes manifest entries
 * against themselves, which proves the zip matches its manifest, never
 * that the payload is self-consistent.
 *
 * Pure classification — no fs, no zip, no exec: the caller (ci/release_packs.mjs)
 * extracts the zip and hands over {path, source} records; this CommonJS twin
 * of the builder keeps the decisions unit-testable in the dmtools runner
 * (same split as ci/pack_release_guard.cjs).
 *
 * Known limit (documented, gh-812 test plan): dynamically assembled requires
 * (`require(prefix + name + '.js')`) cannot be resolved statically and are
 * ignored. The require that broke the incident was a string literal, and
 * every require in this repo's packed code is. Comment/JSdoc text is NOT
 * stripped — the runtime resolver union (see resolveRequireCandidates) kept
 * every doc example in this repo resolvable, and stripping risks missing a
 * real require swallowed by a misdetected regex literal.
 */

/** Literal relative require: require('./a.js'), require ("../b/c.js"). */

'use strict';
/**
 * Pack-release require sanity gate (gh-812, live incident 2026-10-09).
 *
 * The release self-test demanded by gh-812 AC1/AC3: after a pack zip is
 * built, every literal relative `require('./x')` / `require('../y')` in
 * every packed .js must resolve to a file INSIDE the zip — a pack whose
 * code requires a module the zip does not carry must FAIL the release
 * (exit != 0) before the ledger commit and the publish, not live on the
 * fa runners ("Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js").
 *
 * validatePack() cannot catch this class: it re-hashes manifest entries
 * against themselves, which proves the zip matches its manifest, never
 * that the payload is self-consistent.
 *
 * Pure classification — no fs, no zip, no exec: the caller (ci/release_packs.mjs)
 * extracts the zip and hands over {path, source} records; this CommonJS twin
 * of the builder keeps the decisions unit-testable in the dmtools runner
 * (same split as ci/pack_release_guard.cjs).
 *
 * Known limit (documented, gh-812 test plan): dynamically assembled requires
 * (`require(prefix + name + '.js')`) cannot be resolved statically and are
 * ignored. The require that broke the incident was a string literal, and
 * every require in this repo's packed code is. Comment/JSdoc text is NOT
 * stripped — the runtime resolver union (see resolveRequireCandidates) kept
 * every doc example in this repo resolvable, and stripping risks missing a
 * real require swallowed by a misdetected regex literal.
 */

/** Literal relative require: require('./a.js'), require ("../b/c.js"). */

'use strict';
/**
 * Pack-release require sanity gate (gh-812, live incident 2026-10-09).
 *
 * The release self-test demanded by gh-812 AC1/AC3: after a pack zip is
 * built, every literal relative `require('./x')` / `require('../y')` in
 * every packed .js must resolve to a file INSIDE the zip — a pack whose
 * code requires a module the zip does not carry must FAIL the release
 * (exit != 0) before the ledger commit and the publish, not live on the
 * fa runners ("Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js").
 *
 * validatePack() cannot catch this class: it re-hashes manifest entries
 * against themselves, which proves the zip matches its manifest, never
 * that the payload is self-consistent.
 *
 * Pure classification — no fs, no zip, no exec: the caller (ci/release_packs.mjs)
 * extracts the zip and hands over {path, source} records; this CommonJS twin
 * of the builder keeps the decisions unit-testable in the dmtools runner
 * (same split as ci/pack_release_guard.cjs).
 *
 * Known limit (documented, gh-812 test plan): dynamically assembled requires
 * (`require(prefix + name + '.js')`) cannot be resolved statically and are
 * ignored. The require that broke the incident was a string literal, and
 * every require in this repo's packed code is. Comment/JSdoc text is NOT
 * stripped — the runtime resolver union (see resolveRequireCandidates) kept
 * every doc example in this repo resolvable, and stripping risks missing a
 * real require swallowed by a misdetected regex literal.
 */

/** Literal relative require: require('./a.js'), require ("../b/c.js"). */

### What changed Check-run stamps no longer interpolate run-derived text into a shell string. `stampValidationChecksForModule` now builds the Checks-API request body as JSON (`{name, head_sha, status, conclusion?, details_url?, output:{title, summary}}`), writes it to a temp file, posts it with `gh api -X POST repos/{o}/{r}/check-runs --input `, and deletes the file in `finally`. A job named `Lockfile smoke (${{ matrix.os }} release)` therefore reaches dash only as JSON payload bytes — the command string carries zero untrusted bytes, so `Bad substitution` (exit 2, missing stamps, blocked PRs) cannot recur. Transport + helpers live in a new `js/common/checkRunStamp.js`. ### Key decisions - Temp-file JSON body (`--input`) instead of escaping: JSON preserves `${{ }}`, `$(id)`, backticks, `"`, `\`, newlines byte-for-byte (AC1); the same gh-960 PR-body precedent `scm.js` already uses. Only the fixed repo path and a digits-only `/tmp/sm-check-run--.json` path ever touch the shell (AC2). - Temp file deleted in `finally` — on success AND failure (AC3); an unwritable temp dir warns and skips exactly like the old failure mode (E2); summary > 65,535 chars truncates with a marker, never rejected (E1). - `stampLinkBlock` dropped its legacy `"` → `'` mangling — the body must be byte-for-byte, and quotes are safe inside JSON. - AC5 audit of `cli_execute_command` sites interpolating PR/run-derived text — all converted through ONE `shellQuote` (re-exported from `factory/token_usage.js` via `checkRunStamp.js`): - `dispatchCiWorkflow` `--ref ` (validate-arm CI dispatch) — was bare unquoted; - silent-update chain (classic): `--branch ` + push refspec — was bare; - silent-update chain (fork, gh-1070): `git checkout -B ` + `HEAD:` refspec — was bare; - gh-757 ghost dispatch — inline `'`-escaping normalized to the shared helper (byte-identical output); - gh-857 placeholder conclusion PATCH — `details_url` (run-derived URL) + `output[summary]` values now shellQuote'd; - gh-998 zombie-sweep PATCH — fixed-literal summary moved to the same helper so the shape cannot regress. - Audited and left as-is (no untrusted bytes): probe calls keyed on config `ciWorkflow`, hex head SHAs, numeric run/check-run ids; local-teammate runner (Jira key + config values); factory-state transport (already shellQuote'd); zombie/gh-848 PATCH summaries (fixed literals); stderr-file paths (sanitized at creation). - DRY path unchanged (AC4): same `[dry] stamp …` log, no file, no command. ### How to verify ```bash dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json # stamp + hostile-string pins dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_checkRunStamp.json # transport unit tests (UT-1..3, E1, E2) dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json # full suite: 4760 passed, 0 failed ``` Real-shell spot check (reproduces the live bug and proves the fix): the old `-f summary="…(${{ matrix.os }})…"` form exits 2 with `Bad substitution` under dash; the new `--input` form posts the body byte-for-byte, and a shellQuote'd `--ref 'ai/g'\''h-50;$(touch /tmp/pwn)'` dispatch expands nothing.

E1: truncate summary at 65,535] BODY --> FW[file_write /tmp/sm-check-run-N.json] FW --> CLI[gh api -X POST repos/o/r/check-runs --input tmpfile
zero untrusted bytes] CLI --> DEL[file_delete in finally — success AND failure] CLI -->|throws| WARN[warn and skip — next check name] ```

A job named `Lockfile smoke (${{ matrix.os }} release)` therefore reaches dash only as JSON payload bytes — the command string carries zero untrusted bytes, so `Bad substitution` (exit 2, missing stamps, blocked PRs) cannot recur. Transport + helpers live in a new `js/common/checkRunStamp.js`. ### Key decisions - Temp-file JSON body (`--input`) instead of escaping: JSON preserves `${{ }}`, `$(id)`, backticks, `"`, `\`, newlines byte-for-byte (AC1); the same gh-960 PR-body precedent `scm.js` already uses. Only the fixed repo path and a digits-only `/tmp/sm-check-run--.json` path ever touch the shell (AC2). - Temp file deleted in `finally` — on success AND failure (AC3); an unwritable temp dir warns and skips exactly like the old failure mode (E2); summary > 65,535 chars truncates with a marker, never rejected (E1). - `stampLinkBlock` dropped its legacy `"` → `'` mangling — the body must be byte-for-byte, and quotes are safe inside JSON. - AC5 audit of `cli_execute_command` sites interpolating PR/run-derived text — all converted through ONE `shellQuote` (re-exported from `factory/token_usage.js` via `checkRunStamp.js`): - `dispatchCiWorkflow` `--ref ` (validate-arm CI dispatch) — was bare unquoted; - silent-update chain (classic): `--branch ` + push refspec — was bare; - silent-update chain (fork, gh-1070): `git checkout -B ` + `HEAD:` refspec — was bare; - gh-757 ghost dispatch — inline `'`-escaping normalized to the shared helper (byte-identical output); - gh-857 placeholder conclusion PATCH — `details_url` (run-derived URL) + `output[summary]` values now shellQuote'd; - gh-998 zombie-sweep PATCH — fixed-literal summary moved to the same helper so the shape cannot regress. - Audited and left as-is (no untrusted bytes): probe calls keyed on config `ciWorkflow`, hex head SHAs, numeric run/check-run ids; local-teammate runner (Jira key + config values); factory-state transport (already shellQuote'd); zombie/gh-848 PATCH summaries (fixed literals); stderr-file paths (sanitized at creation). - DRY path unchanged (AC4): same `[dry] stamp …` log, no file, no command. ### How to verify ```bash dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json # stamp + hostile-string pins dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_checkRunStamp.json # transport unit tests (UT-1..3, E1, E2) dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json # full suite: 4760 passed, 0 failed ``` Real-shell spot check (reproduces the live bug and proves the fix): the old `-f summary="…(${{ matrix.os }})…"` form exits 2 with `Bad substitution` under dash; 'use strict';
/**
 * Pack-release require sanity gate (gh-812, live incident 2026-10-09).
 *
 * The release self-test demanded by gh-812 AC1/AC3: after a pack zip is
 * built, every literal relative `require('./x')` / `require('../y')` in
 * every packed .js must resolve to a file INSIDE the zip — a pack whose
 * code requires a module the zip does not carry must FAIL the release
 * (exit != 0) before the ledger commit and the publish, not live on the
 * fa runners ("Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js").
 *
 * validatePack() cannot catch this class: it re-hashes manifest entries
 * against themselves, which proves the zip matches its manifest, never
 * that the payload is self-consistent.
 *
 * Pure classification — no fs, no zip, no exec: the caller (ci/release_packs.mjs)
 * extracts the zip and hands over {path, source} records; this CommonJS twin
 * of the builder keeps the decisions unit-testable in the dmtools runner
 * (same split as ci/pack_release_guard.cjs).
 *
 * Known limit (documented, gh-812 test plan): dynamically assembled requires
 * (`require(prefix + name + '.js')`) cannot be resolved statically and are
 * ignored. The require that broke the incident was a string literal, and
 * every require in this repo's packed code is. Comment/JSdoc text is NOT
 * stripped — the runtime resolver union (see resolveRequireCandidates) kept
 * every doc example in this repo resolvable, and stripping risks missing a
 * real require swallowed by a misdetected regex literal.
 */

'use strict';
/**
 * Pack-release require sanity gate (gh-812, live incident 2026-10-09).
 *
 * The release self-test demanded by gh-812 AC1/AC3: after a pack zip is
 * built, every literal relative `require('./x')` / `require('../y')` in
 * every packed .js must resolve to a file INSIDE the zip — a pack whose
 * code requires a module the zip does not carry must FAIL the release
 * (exit != 0) before the ledger commit and the publish, not live on the
 * fa runners ("Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js").
 *
 * validatePack() cannot catch this class: it re-hashes manifest entries
 * against themselves, which proves the zip matches its manifest, never
 * that the payload is self-consistent.
 *
 * Pure classification — no fs, no zip, no exec: the caller (ci/release_packs.mjs)
 * extracts the zip and hands over {path, source} records; this CommonJS twin
 * of the builder keeps the decisions unit-testable in the dmtools runner
 * (same split as ci/pack_release_guard.cjs).
 *
 * Known limit (documented, gh-812 test plan): dynamically assembled requires
 * (`require(prefix + name + '.js')`) cannot be resolved statically and are
 * ignored. The require that broke the incident was a string literal, and
 * every require in this repo's packed code is. Comment/JSdoc text is NOT
 * stripped — the runtime resolver union (see resolveRequireCandidates) kept
 * every doc example in this repo resolvable, and stripping risks missing a
 * real require swallowed by a misdetected regex literal.
 */

/** Literal relative require: require('./a.js'), require ("../b/c.js"). */

 * ignored. The require that broke the incident was a string literal, and
 * every require in this repo's packed code is. Comment/JSdoc text is NOT
 * stripped — the runtime resolver union (see resolveRequireCandidates) kept
 * every doc example in this repo resolvable, and stripping risks missing a

 * every require in this repo's packed code is. Comment/JSdoc text is NOT
 * stripped — the runtime resolver union (see resolveRequireCandidates) kept
 * every doc example in this repo resolvable, and stripping risks missing a

 * built, every literal relative `require('./x')` / `require('../y')` in
 * every packed .js must resolve to a file INSIDE the zip — a pack whose
 * code requires a module the zip does not carry must FAIL the release
 * (exit != 0) before the ledger commit and the publish, not live on the
 * fa runners ("Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js").
 *
 * validatePack() cannot catch this class: it re-hashes manifest entries
 * against themselves, which proves the zip matches its manifest, never
 * that the payload is self-consistent.
 *
 * Pure classification — no fs, no zip, no exec: the caller (ci/release_packs.mjs)
 * extracts the zip and hands over {path, source} records; this CommonJS twin
 * of the builder keeps the decisions unit-testable in the dmtools runner
 * (same split as ci/pack_release_guard.cjs).
 *
 * Known limit (documented, gh-812 test plan): dynamically assembled requires
 * (`require(prefix + name + '.js')`) cannot be resolved statically and are
 * ignored. The require that broke the incident was a string literal, and
 * every require in this repo's packed code is. Comment/JSdoc text is NOT
 * stripped — the runtime resolver union (see resolveRequireCandidates) kept
 * every doc example in this repo resolvable, and stripping risks missing a
 * real require swallowed by a misdetected regex literal.

 * every packed .js must resolve to a file INSIDE the zip — a pack whose

 *
 * validatePack() cannot catch this class: it re-hashes manifest entries
 * against themselves, which proves the zip matches its manifest, never
 * that the payload is self-consistent.

 * Pure classification — no fs, no zip, no exec: the caller (ci/release_packs.mjs)
 * extracts the zip and hands over {path, source} records; this CommonJS twin

 *
 * Known limit (documented, gh-812 test plan): dynamically assembled requires
 * (`require(prefix + name + '.js')`) cannot be resolved statically and are
 * ignored. The require that broke the incident was a string literal, and
 * every require in this repo's packed code is. Comment/JSdoc text is NOT
 * stripped — the runtime resolver union (see resolveRequireCandidates) kept
 * every doc example in this repo resolvable, and stripping risks missing a

'use strict';
/**
 * Pack-release require sanity gate (gh-812, live incident 2026-10-09).
 *
 * The release self-test demanded by gh-812 AC1/AC3: after a pack zip is
 * built, every literal relative `require('./x')` / `require('../y')` in
 * every packed .js must resolve to a file INSIDE the zip — a pack whose
 * code requires a module the zip does not carry must FAIL the release
 * (exit != 0) before the ledger commit and the publish, not live on the
 * fa runners ("Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js").
 *
 * validatePack() cannot catch this class: it re-hashes manifest entries
 * against themselves, which proves the zip matches its manifest, never
 * that the payload is self-consistent.
 *
 * Pure classification — no fs, no zip, no exec: the caller (ci/release_packs.mjs)
 * extracts the zip and hands over {path, source} records; this CommonJS twin
 * of the builder keeps the decisions unit-testable in the dmtools runner
 * (same split as ci/pack_release_guard.cjs).
 *
 * Known limit (documented, gh-812 test plan): dynamically assembled requires
 * (`require(prefix + name + '.js')`) cannot be resolved statically and are
 * ignored. The require that broke the incident was a string literal, and
 * every require in this repo's packed code is. Comment/JSdoc text is NOT
 * stripped — the runtime resolver union (see resolveRequireCandidates) kept
 * every doc example in this repo resolvable, and stripping risks missing a
 * real require swallowed by a misdetected regex literal.
 */

A job named `Lockfile smoke (${{ matrix.os }} release)` therefore reaches dash only as JSON payload bytes — the command string carries zero untrusted bytes, so `Bad substitution` (exit 2, missing stamps, blocked PRs) cannot recur. Transport + helpers live in a new `js/common/checkRunStamp.js`. ### Key decisions - Temp-file JSON body (`--input`) instead of escaping: JSON preserves `${{ }}`, `$(id)`, backticks, `"`, `\`, newlines byte-for-byte (AC1); the same gh-960 PR-body precedent `scm.js` already uses. Only the fixed repo path and a digits-only `/tmp/sm-check-run--.json` path ever touch the shell (AC2). - Temp file deleted in `finally` — on success AND failure (AC3); an unwritable temp dir warns and skips exactly like the old failure mode (E2); summary > 65,535 chars truncates with a marker, never rejected (E1). - `stampLinkBlock` dropped its legacy `"` → `'` mangling — the body must be byte-for-byte, and quotes are safe inside JSON. - AC5 audit of `cli_execute_command` sites interpolating PR/run-derived text — all converted through ONE `shellQuote` (re-exported from `factory/token_usage.js` via `checkRunStamp.js`): - `dispatchCiWorkflow` `--ref ` (validate-arm CI dispatch) — was bare unquoted; - silent-update chain (classic): `--branch ` + push refspec — was bare; - silent-update chain (fork, gh-1070): `git checkout -B ` + `HEAD:` refspec — was bare; - gh-757 ghost dispatch — inline `'`-escaping normalized to the shared helper (byte-identical output); local-teammate runner (Jira key + config values); factory-state transport (already shellQuote'd); zombie/gh-848 PATCH summaries (fixed literals); stderr-file paths (sanitized at creation). - DRY path unchanged (AC4): same `[dry] stamp …` log, no file, no command. ### How to verify ```bash dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json # stamp + hostile-string pins dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_checkRunStamp.json # transport unit tests (UT-1..3, E1, E2) dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json # full suite: 4760 passed, 0 failed ``` Real-shell spot check (reproduces the live bug and proves the fix): the old `-f summary="…(${{ matrix.os }})…"` form exits 2 with `Bad substitution` under dash;
